  Line or code reference: line 1260 — the REVIEWER_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED bullet, new sentence introduced by this PR: "every failback target keeps a 1M+ token window because reviewer prompts regularly exceed 250K tokens"
  Problem: The claim is false for two of the six live mappings listed in the same sentence. scripts/codex_model_catalog.json line 27 sets "context_window": 200000 for minimax/minimax-m2.5 (the minimax/minimax-m3 -> minimax/minimax-m2.5 target), and line 267 sets "context_window": 128000 for deepseek/deepseek-v3.2 (the deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro -> deepseek/deepseek-v3.2 target). Only the three new mappings added by this PR (grok-4.3, glm-5.3-flashx, gemini-3-flash-preview at catalog lines 904, 874, and 87) are actually 1M+.
  Why it fails at runtime: The sentence's own rationale ("reviewer prompts regularly exceed 250K tokens") is exactly the Mistral failure mode this PR removes — a failback dispatch to deepseek-v3.2 (128K) or minimax-m2.5 (200K) against a 250K–400K reviewer prompt overflows the window. Operators reading agents.md (the canonical architecture doc inlined into every unattended prompt) will believe all six failback targets are safe for full-size reviewer prompts when two are not. The fix is to scope the claim to the three new mappings (as the changelog fragment's For-contributors section already does correctly) or re-word it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
